enrichment.headline: Ratifies $7,800 more for brush seals on Nutrition Services dock doors from Commercial Door Solutions
enrichment.summary: The Board is ratifying (approving after the fact) $7,800 more for Commercial Door Solutions of Napa to install brush seals that cover gaps around loading dock levelers and door frames for the Nutrition Services Department. The agreement's cap rises from $16,600 to $24,400. The term is unchanged, December 12, 2024 to June 30, 2025.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Amendment No. 1, Services Agreement 2024-2025 - Commercial Door Solutions - Nutrition Services Department

enrichment.headline: Adds $136,000 for Brigaid to train Nutrition Services staff in scratch cooking at the central kitchen
enrichment.summary: The Board is approving $136,000 more for Brigaid LLC of Middletown, Connecticut to coach and train Nutrition Services staff in scratch cooking at the Central Production Kitchen, including its large-batch cook-chill line and cold prep areas. The agreement's cap rises from $114,000 to $250,000. The period is unchanged, January 1 to June 30, 2025.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Amendment No. 1, Services Agreement 2024-2025 - Brigaid, LLC - Nutrition Services Department

enrichment.headline: Adds $326,840 for Foster Farms chicken wings and strips in school meals, raising the cap to $600,000
enrichment.summary: The Board is approving $326,840 more for Foster Farms, LLC to supply chicken wings and 2-ounce grilled chicken strips for the K-12 meal program. This part of an earlier request for proposals (RFP #24-151NS) was awarded to Foster Farms. The agreement's cap rises from $273,160 to $600,000, and the term is unchanged, July 1, 2024 to June 30, 2025.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Amendment No. 1, Award - RFP #24-151NS (In Part) - Specialty Proteins K-12 Meal Program For Nutrition Services - Foster Farms, LLC - Nutrition Services Department

enrichment.headline: Adds $450,000 for Pacific Rim Produce fresh fruits and vegetables, raising the cap to $2.35M
enrichment.summary: The Board is approving $450,000 more for Pacific Rim Produce of Alameda to supply additional fresh fruits and vegetables for the Nutrition Services Department. The agreement's cap rises from $1,900,000 to $2,350,000. The term is unchanged, July 1, 2024 to June 30, 2025, and is labeled Renewal Option No. 1.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Amendment No. 2, Agreement for Fresh Fruits and Vegetables - Pacific Rim Produce - Nutrition Services Department

enrichment.headline: Awards Tulum Innovative Engineering $312,009 for asphalt, play matting and roof work at Jefferson center
enrichment.summary: The Board is approving a construction agreement with Tulum Innovative Engineering, Inc. of Oakland for $312,009, which includes a $35,000 contingency. The work is replacing asphalt with 3 inches of hot mix asphalt, replacing damaged play matting, and replacing roof eaves at Jefferson Child Development Center. Tulum was the lowest responsive bidder, and work is expected to start June 5, 2025 and finish within 60 days, by August 5, 2025.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
items.title: Agreement Between Owner and Contractor - Tulum Innovative Engineering, Inc. - Jefferson Child Development Center Site Improvements Project - Buildings & Grounds Department

enrichment.headline: Ratifies $1,475 for B SAFE to inspect and test playground equipment at Burbank Child Development Center
enrichment.summary: The Board is ratifying (approving after the fact) a $1,475 lump-sum agreement with B SAFE Playground Inspection Services, Inc. of Sunland. The company is performing impact testing and inspections of playground structures at Burbank Child Development Center as part of its site improvements project. Work was scheduled to start April 24, 2025 and last until June 30, 2025.

vendor.name: B SAFE Playground Inspection Services, Inc.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
items.title: General Services Agreement – B SAFE Playground Inspection Services, Inc. – Sites Improvement Project at Burbank Child Development Center - Division of Facilities Planning and Management

enrichment.headline: Authorizes Alameda County to collect the district's 2025-26 bond and parcel taxes on property tax bills
enrichment.summary: The Board is approving a Proposition 218 certification (formerly called the Certification and Mutual Indemnification Agreement) with the County of Alameda. It allows the county to collect the district's 2025-2026 bond and parcel taxes on secured property tax bills. The text states no dollar amount.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: 25-Proposition 218 Certification - County of Alameda - Collection of District Bond and Parcel Taxes - Fiscal Year 2025-2026

enrichment.headline: Ratifies up to $10,000 for MyPath to train 45 OUSD staff to teach financial literacy
enrichment.summary: The Board is ratifying (approving after the fact) a services agreement and a data sharing agreement with MyPath of San Francisco. For up to $10,000, MyPath will lead a financial literacy train-the-trainer program for 45 OUSD teachers and staff from May 15 to December 31, 2025. The data sharing agreement sets rules for sharing student data with MyPath and for protecting it, from September 1, 2024 to December 31, 2025.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Services Agreement 2024-2025 and Data Sharing Agreement - MyPath - High School Linked Learning Office

enrichment.headline: Extends East Bay Art Therapy's $37,400 school art therapy contract to June 30, 2025 with no added cost
enrichment.summary: The Board is ratifying (approving after the fact) a longer end date for East Bay Art Therapy's contract, moving it from May 30 to June 30, 2025. The provider offers art therapy in groups of 10 to 15 students at Dewey Academy, Ralph J Bunche Academy and Street Academy, and trains Dewey students to lead peer art sessions. The amount stays the same at $37,400.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Amendment No. 1, Services Agreement 2024-2025 - East Bay Art Therapy - Community Schools and Student Services Department

enrichment.headline: Adds $11,000 for Black Cultural Zone summer assemblies for young children and extends the term to June 30
enrichment.summary: The Board is approving $11,000 more for Black Cultural Zone Community Development to put on six interactive summer assemblies or concerts for Bridge to Kindergarten and transitional kindergarten students. The agreement's cap rises from $27,820 to $38,820, and the end date moves from June 20 to June 30, 2025.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Amendment No. 2, Services Agreement 2024-2025 - Black Cultural Zone Community Development - Community Schools and Student Services Department

enrichment.headline: Extends Black Cultural Zone's $52,690 podcasting classes contract to June 30, 2025 at no added cost
enrichment.summary: The Board is approving a longer end date for Black Cultural Zone Community Development's agreement to run summer learning and after-school podcasting classes for 20 students. The end date moves from May 30 to June 30, 2025. The amount stays at a cap of $52,690.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Amendment No. 1, Services Agreement 2024-2025 - Black Cultural Zone Community Development - Community Schools and Student Services Department

enrichment.headline: Ratifies up to $5,000 for National Equity Project leadership sessions at Elmhurst United Middle School
enrichment.summary: The Board is ratifying (approving after the fact) an agreement with the National Equity Project of Oakland for 3 to 4 "Leading for Equity" sessions for school leaders at Elmhurst United Middle School, plus follow-up one-on-one sessions with each leader. The sessions aim to align on the school's vision and build skills in using an equity lens to lead teams. The cost is up to $5,000 for June 16 to June 30, 2025.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Services Agreement 2024-2025 - National Equity Project - Elmhurst United Middle School

enrichment.headline: Pays Sown to Grow up to $297,000 for a student wellness check-in platform and coaching in all schools
enrichment.summary: The Board is approving an agreement with Sown to Grow of Oakland for software licenses and support that let students do a weekly emotional check-in and wellness surveys. It also covers training and coaching for teachers and principals, a social-emotional learning screener and curriculum, and reports for administrators, rolled out in all TK-12 schools. The term is August 1, 2025 to June 1, 2026, at up to $297,000.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Services Agreement 2024-2025 - Sown to Grow - Multi-Tiered Support Systems (MTSS) Department

enrichment.headline: Hires Jewish Community Center of the East Bay to run after-school programs at 3 sites for up to $3.6M
enrichment.summary: The Board is approving a three-year master contract with the Jewish Community Center of the East Bay of Berkeley to serve as lead agency for after-school programs at Hintil Kuu Ca Preschool, Joaquin Miller Elementary School and Thornhill Elementary School. The programs include coordination, academic help, homework support, student supervision and enrichment. The contract runs July 1, 2025 to July 31, 2028 for up to $3,600,000 in total.

vendor.name: Jewish Community Center of the East Bay

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Expanded Learning Programs After School Program Master Contract 2025-2028 - Jewish Community Center of the East Bay - Named Sites - Community Schools and Student Services Department

enrichment.headline: Ratifies up to $17,848 for International Rescue Committee's human trafficking prevention education work
enrichment.summary: The Board is ratifying (approving after the fact) an agreement with the International Rescue Committee of Oakland, one of the nonprofit partners required by the federal Human Trafficking Youth Prevention Education grant. The group works with OUSD project staff to build the capacity to teach human trafficking prevention to teachers, staff, community members, caregivers and students. The cost is up to $17,848 for April 1 to June 30, 2025.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Services Agreement 2024-2025 - International Rescue Committee (IRC) - Community Schools and Student Services Department

enrichment.headline: Hires Think Together to run after-school programs at 4 sites for up to $5.12M through July 2028
enrichment.summary: The Board is approving a three-year master contract with Think Together of Santa Ana to serve as lead agency for after-school programs at Carl B. Munck Elementary School, Claremont Middle School, Edna Brewer Middle School and Montera Middle School. The programs include coordination, academic help, homework support, student supervision and enrichment. The contract runs July 1, 2025 to July 31, 2028 for up to $5,123,238.99 in total.

items.fundingSource: After School Education and Safety Grant, Expanded Learning Opportunities Program

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Expanded Learning Programs After School Program Master Contract 2025-2028 - Think Together - Named Sites - Community Schools and Student Services Department

enrichment.headline: Ratifies a no-cost pilot of OpenLiteracy's reading program for up to 730 students at 27 schools
enrichment.summary: The Board is ratifying (approving after the fact) a no-cost services agreement and a data sharing agreement with OpenLiteracy of Pittsburgh. OpenLiteracy will provide its Tier III reading pilot to up to 730 students at 27 district school sites at no cost to the district. The data sharing agreement sets rules for sharing student data with OpenLiteracy and protecting it. Both run July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: No Cost Services Agreement and Data Sharing Agreement - OpenLiteracy - Academics and Instruction Department

enrichment.headline: Pays The Teaching Well up to $55,000 for coaching of Network 4 principals and its superintendent
enrichment.summary: The Board is approving an agreement with The Teaching Well of Oakland to provide twice-monthly executive coaching for the principals and the superintendent of Elementary Network 4, along with leadership coaching. The cost is up to $55,000. The agreement period began July 1, 2024, before this vote, and ends June 30, 2025.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Services Agreement 2024-2025 - The Teaching Well – Elementary Network 4

enrichment.headline: Ratifies a no-cost Ignite Reading virtual tutoring program for 720 students at 23 schools
enrichment.summary: The Board is ratifying (approving after the fact) a no-cost services agreement and a data sharing agreement with Ignite Reading of San Francisco. Ignite Reading will give 720 students at 23 schools 15 minutes a day, 5 days a week, of one-on-one virtual reading skills instruction with a trained tutor, at no cost to the district. The data sharing agreement sets rules for sharing student data and protecting it. Both run July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: No Cost Services Agreement and Data Sharing Agreement - Ignite Reading - Academics and Instruction Department

enrichment.headline: Accepts $11,506 from Oakland Public Education Fund for Skyline High School's Music in the Parks trip
enrichment.summary: The Board is approving a grant agreement in which the district accepts $11,506 from the Oakland Public Education Fund. The money supports transportation and attendance for Skyline High School music students in the Music in the Parks project. The grant period is April 30 to June 30, 2025.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Grant Agreement - Oakland Public Education Fund - Music in the Parks - Skyline High School

enrichment.headline: Pays Museum of Children's Art up to $3,050 for visual art workshops at a summer learning institute
enrichment.summary: The Board is approving an agreement with the Museum of Children's Art of Oakland to work with the Extended Learning Office team to develop and run workshops based on the state's visual art standards and the theme of the Expanded Learning Summer Institute. The cost is up to $3,050 for July 3 to July 31, 2025.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Services Agreement - Museum of Children's Art - After School Program - Community Schools and Student Services Department

enrichment.headline: Pays Be the Change Consulting up to $11,725 to train after-school staff on state quality standards
enrichment.summary: The Board is approving an agreement with Be the Change Consulting of Oakland to work with the Extended Learning Office team to design and run several training sessions based on California Department of Education after-school quality standards. The cost is up to $11,725 for July 2 to July 31, 2025.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Services Agreement - Be the Change Consulting - After School Program - Community Schools and Student Services Department

enrichment.headline: Ratifies McCormick Barstow law firm contract for up to $110,000 per year through June 2028
enrichment.summary: The Board is ratifying (approving after the fact) a memorandum of understanding and engagement policy and a data sharing agreement with the McCormick Barstow law firm. The firm will provide legal services on civil lawsuits and other matters as the Legal Department requests, for up to $110,000 per fiscal year. The term is July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2028, and the data sharing agreement covers how student data is shared and protected.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Memorandum of Understanding and Engagement Policy and Data Sharing Agreement - McCormick Barstow Law Firm - General Counsel

enrichment.headline: Updates the lease for Kipp Bridge Charter School's use of the Lafayette Elementary campus
enrichment.summary: The Board is approving a second amendment to the ground lease and joint use agreement with Kipp Bridge Charter School for the Lafayette Elementary School campus. It adds a legal description of the property, reflecting updated boundaries after the district's 2021 property exchange with the City, and clarifies the initial rent credit. No dollar amount is stated, and all other terms stay in effect.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Amendment No. 2, Ground Lease - Joint Use Agreement - Kipp Bridge Charter School - @ LaFayette Elementary School Campus

enrichment.headline: Hires Girls, Inc. of Alameda County to run after-school programs at 5 sites for up to $6.79M
enrichment.summary: The Board is approving a three-year master contract with Girls, Inc. of Alameda County to serve as lead agency for after-school programs at Allendale Elementary School, Bella Vista Elementary School, Bridges Academy, Burkhalter Elementary School and Horace Man Elementary School. The programs include coordination, academic help, homework support, student supervision and enrichment. The contract runs July 1, 2025 to July 31, 2028 for up to $6,789,181.95 in total.

items.fundingSource: After School Education and Safety Grant, Expanded Learning Opportunities Program

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Expanded Learning Programs After School Program Master Contract 2025-2028 - Girls, Inc. of Alameda County - Community Schools and Student Services Department

enrichment.headline: Raises ACC Environmental's survey contract for a Maxwell Park campus classroom building to $24,442.50
enrichment.summary: The Board is approving an amendment for ACC Environmental Consultants, Inc. of Oakland, which is surveying the new classroom building at the Maxwell Park campus for asbestos and lead before renovation. The agreement's cap rises from $10,169.50 to $24,442.50, and the end date moves from June 30, 2025 to June 30, 2028 (1,096 more days). The text prints the added amount as $14,727,50, which does not match the change in the cap.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
items.title: Amendment No. 1, General Services Agreement – ACC Environmental Consultants, Inc. – MLA at Maxwell Park Campus New Classroom Bldg. Modernization Project – Division of Facilities Planning and Management

enrichment.headline: Awards Deco Tech Systems $56,948 to install door intercom systems at 4 schools
enrichment.summary: The Board is approving an agreement with Deco Tech Systems, Inc. of Walnut Creek for $56,948.46, which includes a $5,176.77 contingency requested by the district. Deco Tech will install AIPhone door entry intercom systems at Allendale Elementary School, Sequoia Elementary School, Montclair Elementary School and Roosevelt Middle School. It was the lowest responsive, responsible bidder, and work is expected to run June 5 to September 3, 2025.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
items.title: Agreement Between Owner and Contractor – Deco Tech Systems, Inc. – Various Sites Door Entry Systems Upgrades Group 3 Project- Division of Facilities Planning and Management

enrichment.headline: Hires Geo-Engineering Solutions for $57,288 of soil studies for solar projects at 5 sites
enrichment.summary: The Board is approving an agreement with Geo-Engineering Solutions, Inc. of San Ramon for $57,288, which includes a $5,208 contingency for additional services. The firm will provide geotechnical (soil and ground) consulting for the Solar Photovoltaics Phase 2 and 3 Project at Horace Mann Elementary School, Oakland Academy of Knowledge, Madison Park Academy, Stonehurst Elementary School and Laurel Child Development Center. Work is scheduled from June 5, 2025 to April 30, 2026.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
items.title: Agreement for Engineering Services – Geo-Engineering Solutions, Inc. – Solar Photovoltaics Phase 2 & 3 Project - Division of Facilities Planning and Management - Division of Facilities Planning and Management

enrichment.headline: Adds $68.4M to Overaa's Roosevelt Middle School modernization contract, bringing the total to $75.4M
enrichment.summary: The Board is approving Amendment No. 3 to the lease-leaseback construction contract with C. Overaa & Company of Richmond. It sets the Guaranteed Maximum Price for Phase III construction of the Roosevelt Middle School Modernization Project. The contract cap rises from $7,014,345 to $75,411,550, and the end date moves from July 31, 2027 to September 30, 2029. The text says this is within the Board-approved project budget.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
items.title: Amendment No. 3, Award of a Lease-Leaseback Contract – C. Overaa & Company – Roosevelt Middle School Modernization Project– Division of Facilities Planning and Management

enrichment.headline: Adds $6,845.70 for Tulum Innovative Engineering's Cole Data Center parking lot and gate work
enrichment.summary: The Board is approving $6,845.70 more for Tulum Innovative Engineering, Inc. of Oakland for added construction on the Cole Data Center Move Project, including removing and relocating the staff parking lot, a rolling gate pedestal and access control systems. The agreement's cap rises from $36,507.74 to $43,353.44, and the end date moves from July 31 to December 31, 2025 (153 more days).

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report
